newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Metal prices to hit RTZ-CRA profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Metal prices to hit RTZ-CRA profit.

text.p: Depressed metal prices will have hit 1996 profits at RTZ-CRA, but analysts predict a pick-up in 1997 results of the Anglo-Australian mining group.
RTZ-CRA, formed through a merger late in 1995, releases its full 1996 figures on Thursday.
Analysts' forecasts for net adjusted earnings range between $1.06 billion and $1.14 billion compared with $1.44 billion the year before.
The company was hit particularly hard by a slump in copper, RTZ-CRA's main metal.
Prices slumped an average 22.7 percent last year due to general oversupply and the trading crisis triggered by the huge losses piled up by Sumitomo's rogue trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
Copper was squeezed up again recently, but analysts believe prices will retreat later this year as supply is seen continuing to exceed world demand.
But industry watchers believe the reverse will be the case for aluminium, another important metal for RTZ-CRA.
Partly through 67 percent stake in Australia's Comalco Ltd, aluminium represented about 18 percent of RTZ-CRA's 1995 turnover and nearly 14 precent of earnings.
Besides an aluminium price improvement, RTZ-CRA should also benefit from smoother operations at its Bingham Canyon copper smelter, which suffered from technical hitches last year.
The smelter in Utah, U.S., became operational in 1995 and is expected to reach full capacity early this year.
Analysts forecast that RTZ-CRA's net earnings this year will rise to between $1.2 to $1.4 billion.
